title: Oncoskill Current State
description: The single source of truth the skill reads at the start of a session instead of relying on chat memory. The user keeps this one living file (e.g. in a Project); the skill reads it at session start and proposes updates to the relevant section at the end. This is the ONE place of memory: medications, labs, decisions, recommendations, windows, documents and so on are SECTIONS of this doc, not separate ledgers. Only two other artifacts are genuinely separate because they differ in shape/audience: the Outreach Ledger (clinic / second-opinion CRM) and the Doctor Share Pack (clean outward dossier). When the skill learns something new, it offers to update the relevant section here rather than inventing a new tracker. None of these clinical fields are asserted by the skill: they only ever hold what the user supplies from their own documents and their care team — restate what is documented, never infer it. All fields are optional except last_updated.

patient.description: Minimal, user-controlled. Keep identifying detail to what the user chooses to store.

label.description: A name or initials the user chooses.

context.description: Who and where, so the skill can adapt instead of assuming. Everything in Oncoskill is example-level and must be adapted to this context and to the care team's instructions over anything bundled.

role.description: Who is using the skill right now: patient / caregiver / both.

country_or_region.description: Country / region, so guidance can be adapted. Bundled regional packs (e.g. Portugal) are examples; laws, insurers and health systems differ by place.

health_system.description: e.g. public / private / mixed / specific insurer — used to route funding and access questions.

language.description: Preferred language(s) for replies and for drafting clinician-facing material.

response_style.description: Preferred shape of replies (see references/core/tone.md). Default conversational; an overloaded user gets a short bottom line regardless.

diagnosis.description: As documented; not asserted by the skill. Restate the diagnosis/stage a signed report documents; never independently infer it.

treatment_phase.description: e.g. diagnosis / staging / treatment-planning / on-treatment / results / survivorship.

important_constraints.description: Hard deadlines, windows, medical constraints, things that must not be forgotten.

emotional_caregiver_context.description: Caregiver load / state — used to calibrate tone and to trigger the caregiver mode.

medications.description: Current and historical medicines, with explicit status, date, and source. Personal dose/schedule come only from the prescription or discharge instructions; package strength is separate. Unresolved conflicts are recorded for the pharmacist/team, never resolved by guessing.

name.description: Name as written (brand or generic). Brands differ by country — verify the active ingredient and strength from the package.

active_ingredient.description: Active ingredient as printed on the package, where known — helps spot hidden duplicates across products.

dose.description: Personal regimen copied verbatim from prescription/discharge instructions; never inferred from box strength or general leaflet dosing.

schedule.description: As prescribed (e.g. 'twice daily', 'as needed for pain'). Only from the prescription; never invented.

reason.description: What it is for, if the user knows.

last_dose.description: When the last dose was taken, if tracked — useful at handovers so a regimen is not doubled up.

next_allowed_dose.description: Only an explicit patient-specific time or instruction from the prescription/discharge plan. Never computed from a generic leaflet.

status_date.description: Date of the documented or reported status change; do not invent.

strength.description: Product strength printed on the package; distinct from the prescribed dose.

source.description: Where this came from (prescription, leaflet, discharge note, the prescribing doctor). Provenance, not assertion.

allergies.description: Drug / substance allergies and intolerances, as the patient reports or a record documents — important context the team and any clinician-facing pack should carry.

reaction.description: What happens (e.g. rash, anaphylaxis), as described.

status.description: confirmed = documented by a clinician / test; reported = patient-stated. Keep the distinction honest.

labs.description: Lab results week-to-week, recorded as the report states them. Read trends over single points; typical thresholds are the team's call, not the skill's. Only interpret a value as low/high when a reference range is actually present — otherwise note it as 'mentioned in the report — worth confirming the range'. Never alter or recall values for a clinician-facing message; use only the numbers the user supplies from their documents.

marker.description: e.g. Hb, neutrophils, platelets, creatinine, ferritin, TSAT, CEA.

value.description: As reported (string to preserve units/operators like '<0.1' faithfully).

reference_range_if_present.description: Only if the report actually prints a range. Absent here means do not call the value high or low.

treatment_day_or_phase.description: Where in treatment this was drawn (e.g. 'day 8 of cycle 2', 'pre-chemoradiation') — needed to read the trend.

decisions.description: Decisions and their rationale, dates, and source. An agreed decision may be reviewed through a second opinion; preserve history and the patient's choice.

who.description: Who made / owns it (the patient remains the final decision-maker).

alternatives.description: Other options that were on the table.

evidence_source_refs.description: What it was based on — documents, guideline references, a claim_id.

can_revisit.description: Whether the user currently wants to revisit this decision. False is not a ban on a later second opinion.

review_date.description: When to look at it again, if relevant.

recommendations.description: Recommendations on the table — both doctor-given and self-found — kept side by side and clearly attributed. A self-found option is something to raise collaboratively as a question, not a verdict on the team; trust the team and verify, and confirm anything self-found against current guidance and the care team before acting.

who_source.description: Where it originated — kept explicit so the two never blur.

source_detail.description: Which doctor / which source, for traceability.

applies_to.description: What situation it applies to (so a general example is not mistaken for a rule for this case).

windows.description: Time-critical medical, administrative, or funding windows. Record actual dates and sources. A clinically acceptable delay must be confirmed for this case; never infer one from a general rule.

what_closes_after.description: What becomes impossible once it passes.

type.description: Kind of window, to route it.

required_action.description: What needs doing, and ideally what to run in parallel now.

fallback.description: The next route if this one closes — never released before the primary is truly secured.

escalation_condition.description: What triggers escalating (a non-reply by a date, a missing confirmation).

documents.description: The documents the user holds, so nothing is lost and a clean share pack can be built fast. Track originals vs working translations separately; keep originals alongside translations. share_safe flags whether it is ready for a clinician-facing pack (stripped of unrelated personal data, internal/emotional notes, and unverified AI hypotheses) — that lives in the Doctor Share Pack, not here.

type.description: e.g. pathology report, discharge note, imaging, consent form, prescription, invoice.

original_or_translation.description: Keep the two distinct; a working translation never replaces the original.

key_content.description: A plain one-liner of what it contains.

share_safe.description: Whether it has been redaction-checked for a clinician-facing pack.

red_flags_given_by_team.description: The specific 'call us / go to emergency if…' triggers this patient's own team has given — recorded verbatim so they take priority over any general list. If one of these happens, route to the care team / emergency now (POLICY.md).

care_team_contacts.description: How to reach the actual care team — including the working channel (a named person / direct line that gets a response), not just a general switchboard. Verify any number before relying on it; details here are the user's own, not bundled examples.

name.description: Person or role (e.g. reference nurse, oncology secretariat).

channel.description: Phone / email / portal — ideally the working channel that actually gets a reply.

hours.description: When reachable, and who to use out of hours.

provenance.description: Audit trail — never silently rewrite history. Append an entry on each meaningful change.

source.description: what prompted it (a document, a visit debrief, a claim_id)
